subject: Request: Temporary capacity exception & proportional remedy allocation
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@crestline.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonathan Park <jonathan.park@crestline.com>
Date: 2025-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Temporary capacity exception request for July launch + remedy proposal

Hi Markus,

Quick note from the ops team at Crestline — our product launch on July 1 is expected to drive a sustained 8-10x traffic spike for the first 4 weeks. Our infra forecast shows a potential service pressure window where Redwood-hosted capacity could be constrained despite our dedicated pool.

We want to request a temporary SLA template exception for July (2025-07-01 to 2025-07-31) that:
- allows for a narrower uptime commitment for batched, compute-bound routes during the burst window (we can accept 99.5% for those routes), and
- applies a proportional monthly service-credit cap instead of full formulaic credits (specifically: cap credits at 5% of the month’s invoice for the July period).

Attached is an updated SOW that calls out the expected request patterns and a technical appendix with peak QPS by route. Can Redwood confirm whether this exception is workable, and if so, outline the template language we should expect? Legal at Crestline is copied for awareness — they prefer the cap to be explicit in the SLA amendment.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — our procurement review window closes next week.

Thanks,
Alyssa Turner
Head of Infrastructure, Crestline Systems
[Attachment: Crestline_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@crestline.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-28T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity exception request for July launch + remedy proposal

Alyssa — thanks for the heads-up and the SOW. Congratulations on the launch.

High level: we can support a timeboxed operational exception for batched/compute-bound routes, but we need to align on:
- exact routes and prefix keys that will be scoped to the exception,
- telemetry/alerts to prove the burst was the cause (we'll need realtime usage exports), and
- an upper bound on credits to protect both sides.

Options we are comfortable proposing back to legal:
1) Temporary Exception + Proportional Remedy: exception period 2025-07-01 to 2025-07-31; uptime floor for scoped routes = 99.5%; remedy calculated per our standard formula but capped at 6% of monthly invoice for July.
2) Hybrid: require pre-scheduled burst window (we lock expected peak days/times in the SOW), maintain normal uptime SLOs for control plane but carve out the listed routes; credits calculated as proportional to duration and impact, capped at 4% if Crestline provides pre-notification and usage exports.

Laura / Ben — can you take a quick pass on legal/contract implications? Specifically: whether we can accept a month-limited cap (option 1) vs. a conditional lower cap that requires pre-notification (option 2). Also, is the 6% ceiling above a workable maximum from a commercial risk perspective?

Action items:
- Alyssa: confirm which routes to carve out (route list or prefix table).
- Crestline legal: confirm cap preference (5% requested vs. options above).
- Laura / Ben: I'll wait for redlines and a brief summary on the worksheet.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-sla-proposal-20250628.docx (docx)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>, Alyssa Turner <alyssa@crestline.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-06-29T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity exception request for July launch + remedy proposal

Markus / Alyssa — looped in after quick review of the ask and the proposal document. A few points from contracts/legal perspective:

1) Scope clarity: we must enumerate the exact API routes or model variants to be in the carveout. Broad language creates downstream ambiguity and is risky. Suggest a table in the amendment listing endpoints + expected traffic profile.

2) Cap mechanics: Crestline’s ask for 5% is reasonable if accompanied by: (a) telemetry exports showing the burst spike attributable to expected user traffic, and (b) an explicit limited timeframe (we like the 1-month box). Internal comfort levels:
- 6% cap if no pre-notification (covers unknown risk),
- 4% cap if Crestline provides a 72-hour pre-notification and rolling usage exports.

3) Latency SLOs: we should keep p90 latency SLOs unchanged. Any latency degradations should be compensated under the standard latency remedy (separate bucket) unless linked to the scoped routes and explicitly carved out.

4) Audit & termination: include a short audit clause allowing Redwood to verify traffic patterns and the ability to revoke the exception if misuse is detected.

I attached a redline draft that integrates option 1 language and includes the conditional 4%/6% caps. If Crestline prefers their 5% number, we'll need sign-off from Finance.

Next steps:
- Alyssa: please confirm whether Crestline will provide pre-notification (72 hrs) and rolling exports.
- Markus / Ben: finance to confirm acceptable ceiling (we should be ready to field a quick ask to accept 5% if the account profile supports it).

Laura Bennett
Sr. Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: SLA_redline_markus_20250629.docx (docx)]

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa@crestline.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonathan Park <jonathan.park@crestline.com>, Crestline Systems Legal <legal@crestline.com>
Date: 2025-07-02T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary capacity exception request for July launch + remedy proposal

Laura / Markus — thanks for the quick review and the thoughtful options. Crestline is prepared to provide 72-hour pre-notifications for the main peak windows and rolling usage exports during July. Given that, our internal preference is the conditional cap (4%).

A couple small asks before we sign:
- Can you add explicit language that the cap applies only to the July period and will not set precedent for future quarters?
- We request a short onboarding checklist in the amendment that confirms the export format and delivery endpoint for telemetry (S3 or secure webhook).

If you can update the redline with those two items, we can route for signature and get the SOW countersigned this week.

Appreciate the partnership — excited to go live.

Best,
Alyssa Turner
Head of Infrastructure, Crestline Systems
[Attachment: none]
